proposed_comments.title: Keep numbered shortcuts aligned with visible items

confidence.rationale: The preserved fix shows that assigning shortcut slots from the complete filtered list lets an off-screen item consume Alt+number after scrolling, which diverges from the visible cues.

proposed_comments.body:
**Affected code:** `src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/ExtViews/ListItemsView.xaml.cs` (`ListItemsView`) and `src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels/NumberedItemShortcuts.cs` (`NumberedItemShortcuts.GetTargets`).

**Problem:** Numbered cues can be assigned from the complete filtered list while activation is invoked after the list has scrolled. An off-screen interactive item can therefore take an Alt+number slot even though no matching visible cue is displayed.

**Why it matters:** Alt+1 can execute or select a different item than the cue the user sees, making keyboard navigation unreliable and potentially invoking an unintended command.

**Suggested change:**
1. Determine numbered-shortcut targets from realized, loaded containers that intersect the list viewport when the numbered cues are enabled.
2. Reuse that same visible-target sequence for both accelerator dispatch and cue rendering, refreshing it after relevant layout and scroll changes.
3. Add focused coverage that scrolls a list before using a numbered shortcut and verifies that the invoked item matches the visible cue.

**Verification:** Build the CmdPal UI project, then verify that Alt+1 and Alt+Shift+1 continue to target the visible numbered item before and after scrolling a list page.
proposed_comments.out_of_diff_reason: The correction coordinates target selection, viewport tracking, cue refresh, and tests across multiple files; it cannot be safely represented by one localized apply-ready suggestion.

proposed_comments.title: Unify localized CmdPal access-key resources

confidence.rationale: The current head introduces separate literal and resource access-key paths, including two Filters entries, so localized XAML and code-behind values can drift.

proposed_comments.body:
**Affected code:** `src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/Controls/CommandBar.xaml`, `src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/Controls/DevRibbon.xaml`, `src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/Controls/FiltersDropDown.xaml.cs`, and `src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/Strings/en-us/Resources.resw`.

**Problem:** The new Settings, Filters, and developer-ribbon access keys are split between literals and distinct resource keys. In particular, separate `FiltersDropDown.AccessKey` and `FiltersDropDown_AccessKey` values can diverge across localized resource files.

**Why it matters:** The mnemonic restored by code-behind can differ from the mnemonic exposed by the localized XAML control, causing inconsistent keyboard behavior in non-English builds.

**Suggested change:**
1. Put each new access key in the existing localized resource workflow used by its XAML control.
2. Use the same resource key/value when code-behind restores a control's access key.
3. Remove duplicate resource contracts after migrating their consumers so translators maintain one value per mnemonic.

**Verification:** Build the CmdPal UI project and verify the Settings, Filters, and developer-ribbon access keys after opening and closing the affected controls with the en-us resources and a localized resource set.
proposed_comments.out_of_diff_reason: The correction requires coordinated XAML, code-behind, and localized-resource edits, so a single localized apply-ready suggestion would be unsafe.
proposed_comments.outOfDiffReason: The correction requires coordinated XAML, code-behind, and localized-resource edits, so a single localized apply-ready suggestion would be unsafe.
